nodes.text: Hello there, young builder! Our world has lost its colors. Grey is swallowing everything. But I believe you can help us bring it back!
Start small. Light drives back the grey. Craft some torches and place them around our village. Here, let me give you a task.
The Dim Barrens grew from the east. Color just drains away there. Ancient beacons once kept the world bright, but they have gone dark.
The beacons need crystal shards and iron to rebuild. Explore, gather, and when you are ready, we will light them together. The world is counting on us!
Wisdom? Of course! Always carry a torch, never trust a cave that giggles, and if a chicken stares at you, stare right back. Blink first and it owns your hat now. Those are the rules.
A story! Once, a brave hero set off to save the whole world, and then... hmm. I forgot the middle part. And the end. Old brains are like buckets with holes. But it was VERY exciting! Trust me.
Hey! Good timing. I am trying to fix up the village but we are short on supplies. Can you help me out?
First things first: you need a crafting table. Four planks in a square. Once you have one, stone tools and proper building become possible.
Nice work! With stone tools you can mine proper stone. Bring me some stone bricks for the walls. They look much better than cobblestone.

choices.label: I will get right on it.

nodes.text: Going GREAT, mostly! I measured twice and cut once, then noticed I was holding the plank upside down. Building is ten percent skill and ninety percent oops. Good old cobblestone never judges me.

Tip one: a door is just a wall that changed its mind. Tip two: if a wall looks wobbly, squint until it looks fine. Tip three: never build a roof while standing ON the roof. I learned that one the bumpy way.
I once built a grand tower! Well, half a tower. The other half is also somewhere. Possibly underground. Possibly in a tree. We do not talk about the tower. The tower does not talk about us either.
Welcome! I study the plants and creatures of our land. The grey has been hard on them too. The animals seem frightened and lost.

choices.label: How can I help the animals?
Do you really talk to plants?

nodes.text: You can befriend them with food! Woolly lambs love berry clusters. Befriend two and use their wool. I think it helps the lambs feel safe.
I make healing stews from mushrooms. The pine forest has plenty, but I am too busy here. Could you collect some for me?
Every single day! The mushrooms are wonderful listeners. The cactus, between us, is a little prickly about feedback. And the flowers? They just blush and say nothing at all.

Oh, they have OPINIONS. The lambs mostly say baa, which means snacks please. The chickens think they are in charge of everything. And between us... the chickens might be right. Do not tell the chickens I said that.
The mushrooms told me a secret, but it was very quiet and also mushroom flavored, so I missed it. The ferns are terribly dramatic. The moss just vibes. The moss always vibes. Be more like the moss.
